function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**The next big festival in the United States (as of June 23 2026)**  
> **Taste of Chicago**  
> • **Dates:** Saturday July 7 – Tuesday July 10, 2026  
> • **Location:** Grant Park, Chicago, Illinois (and surrounding streets)  
> • **What to expect:**  
>   * Over **200 food vendors** showcasing Chicago‑style cuisine (deep‑dish pizza, hot dogs, Italian beef, Korean BBQ, vegan options, etc.)  
>   * Live music from local and national acts across multiple stages (rock, hip‑hop, jazz, electronic, and more).  
>   * Family‑friendly activities: kids’ cooking demos, interactive art installations, and a “Taste of Chicago” food‑truck parade.  
>   * Cultural showcases: Chicago‑based dance troupes, improv comedy, and a “Taste of Chicago” film series featuring short films from local filmmakers.  
> • **Attendance:** Roughly **1.5 million** people over the four‑day span.  
> • **Tickets:** Free entry; food and drinks are purchased at the vendors.  
> • **Transportation:** Public transit (CTA trains and buses) is heavily promoted; bike‑share stations and a temporary “Taste‑of‑Chicago” shuttle service run between the park and nearby hotels.  

---

### Other notable festivals happening soon (after June 23, 2026)

| Festival | Dates | Location | Highlights |
|----------|-------|----------|------------|
| **Summerfest** | July 12 – 24, 2026 | Milwaukee, WI | 8‑day music marathon, 800+ stages, 1.5 M+ attendees |
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | July 20 – 24, 2026 | Manchester, TN | 4‑day festival, 30 k+ attendees, 200+ stages |
| **Comic‑Con International** | July 20 – 23, 2026 | San Diego, CA | 200 k+ visitors, panels, cosplay, exclusive premieres |
| **New York Film Festival** | September 1 – 10, 2026 | New York, NY | 200+ feature films, 50 k+ attendees |
| **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | March 11 – 20, 2026 | Austin, TX | 3‑day music, film, tech conference (already passed for 2026) |

---

### Quick Tips for Planning

| Tip | Why it matters |
|-----|----------------|
| **Book lodging early** | Popular festivals fill up quickly; consider staying in nearby cities if the venue is in a small town. |
| **Check the festival’s COVID‑19 policy** | Some festivals still require proof of vaccination or a negative test. |
| **Use public transit or rideshare** | Parking can be limited and expensive; many festivals offer shuttle services. |
| **Pack light** | Most festivals have strict bag policies; bring only essentials. |
| **Stay hydrated** | Bring a refillable water bottle; many festivals now offer free water stations. |

---
